title: Royal Albert Edward Infirmary failings revealed in damning report

input.lead: The Wigan hospital had one of the country's worst record for A&E waits
input.summary: The Wigan hospital had one of the country's worst record for A&E waits
input.evidence_text: Royal Albert Edward Infirmary failings revealed in damning report - BBC News Image source, Google Image caption, The Royal Albert Edward Infirmary's urgent and emergency care and medical care had been previously rated as "good" by inspectors By Lynette Horsburgh North West Published 2 hours ago Records show a hospital trust is "among the worst in England" for people spending more than 12 hours in the emergency department. More than 900 people faced stays of such length in the month prior to a damning inspection. The Care Quality Commission (CQC) has downgraded urgent and emergency care at Royal Albert Edward Infirmary in Wigan, Greater Manchester, after several concerns were raised over patient care. A warning notice has been issued over the triage system, the identification of sepsis and how those with mental health needs are cared for after the unannounced inspection in May, with "rapid improvements" called for. The trust said it was "working hard" to make improvements. The NHS watchdog previously rated the urgent and emergency care and the medical care at the hospital - which was also inspected - as "good" but has downgraded them both to "requires improvement". Inspectors said the service was not meeting any of its sepsis targets citing two cases where staff had identified potential sepsis and follow up actions had not been completed more than 18 hours later. National guidelines state they should be done within an hour. Inspectors found leaders had not ensured there were dedicated spaces to safely accommodate high-risk young people with mental health needs, with some staff saying they had experienced physical and psychological harm as a result. Inspectors said the physical limitations of the department meant staff could not always respect people's dignity and privacy

The animal welfare charity is proposing to create what it describes as a "one-stop shop" from rescue to recovery for animals most in need on farmland close to Pennington Flash in Leigh, Wigan. Part of the site is just 50 metres (164 ft) away from the Pennington Flash nature reserve. The 15 hectare site is made up of agricultural land, a disused railway embankment and woodland. The document said the development would include clinical veterinary and behavioural facilities, rehabilitation, training and rehoming provision and administration buildings. The report said: "The main building with veterinary services and staff offices, a ferret block and an electrical substation will be located in the central south of the site. "The campus will include a small animals block, a hay barn, cattery blocks and a foul drainage treatment plant." They had undertaken their basic life support training years ago on their initial prison officer training."

Those who pay within 10 days will be eligible for a reduced payment of £700, with the full amount payable within 14 days. The landmark decision is subject to a The move is part of a wider commitment to tackle environmental crime and support the ambitions set out in Manchester's new Fly-tipping and Litter Strategy, which aims to reduce fly-tipping incidents by a third by 2035 Residents have repeatedly said cleaner streets, well-kept parks and action on environmental crime as among their top priorities for the city. Fly-tipping continues to place a significant burden on council resources, drain public money away from essential services and impact the h In 2025-26, Manchester recorded 17,954 fly-tipping incidents, resulting in the removal of more than 5,594 tonnes of waste from across the city. title: Bolton Car Boot Sale

input.lead: Bolton Car Boot Sale at Bolton Car Boot Sale
input.summary: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and t
input.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained.
